title: Model agent handoffs, named waits and review decisions in TLA+
outcome: Model agent handoffs, named waits and review decisions in TLA+
acceptance: A bounded TLA+ model represents review parent, two reviewers, decision owner, scheduler and worker, with explicit work claims, result production, direct messages, mailbox delivery and acknowledgement, named waits and wakes, review-pair completion, resource-slot END and subsequent placement

Safety invariants include: no unnamed wait without an explicit recovery gap; a scheduler slot END is never a finding handoff; send or mailbox acknowledgement alone never proves execution or completion; no duplicate execution after retry or handoff; no completion with required review or evaluation missing; no launch before the current slot holder releases it; one live ordinary owner per work run
The R30 incident is encoded as a regression scenario where pair END reaches only the scheduler and the decision owner must not be treated as notified or the review parent as resumable

Under explicit eventual-delivery and active-participant fairness assumptions, the model checks whether a produced result reaches its named waiter and a released resource reaches the next named waiter; without those assumptions any recovery gap remains explicit
Claude::TLA runs TLC on bounded instances and retains complete spec, configuration, state counts, results and minimized counterexamples, with no unbounded always-works claim

Kimi independently reviews the model against rules-waits-and-wakes and the actual review/test handoff skills; actionable traces produce minimal procedure or skill corrections without watchers, global locks or new gates
The work is sequential after w-7d425bd8df14, changes no production code and does not block or consume current sync build capacity
